lessons.culture: The adhan is called from the minaret five times a day, and the iqamah, said a little later just before the prayer starts, tells everyone to stand in rows. Many masjids in the Hejaz have a separate entrance for women, usually a side door. Someone who arrives late joins the imam at once, then stands and completes the missed rak'ahs after the imam's salaam; afterwards people say تَقَبَّلَ اللهُ and answer مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ.

lessons.culture: Wudu is the washing done before prayer, and every masjid has a wudu area, usually beside the restrooms. Shoes come off at the entrance and go on the rack, clothes should be clean and modest, and phones go on silent so nobody's prayer is disturbed. The qibla is the direction of the Kaaba in Makkah, and a niche called the mihrab often marks it.

lessons.culture: Jumu'ah takes the place of the Dhuhr prayer on Friday and is prayed in congregation after the khutbah. Many people bathe, wear clean clothes and come early, and during the khutbah everyone listens in silence. In a crowded masjid the rows are filled by moving closer together, and afterwards people greet each other with جُمُعَة مُبَارَكَة. Friday is part of the weekend in Saudi Arabia.

lessons.culture: Many masjids run Qur'an circles (7alagaat) for adults and children, often after Maghrib or Fajr, where each student recites from memory to the teacher, who is called أستاذ or شيخ. The mushaf is handled with respect: kept off the floor and returned to its shelf after use. A student who recites well is answered with مَا شَاءَ اللهُ، بَارَكَ اللهُ فِيكَ.

challenge.title: A Visit to the Masjid
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines at the masjid. Ask which prayer is next and when the iqamah is, find the wudu area and the entrance, put your shoes on the rack, find the qibla, silence your phone, and say what you do when you arrive late. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 17, and use فين, إيش and دحين the Hejazi way.
required_elements: A greeting, السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ, and its reply.
A question about the next prayer or the time of the adhan or iqamah, using إيش or إمتى.
A question about the wudu area or the entrance, using فين.
A request about the shoe rack, the prayer rug or the qibla.
A polite request or reply about the phone, using لو سمحت or شكراً.
A missed rak'ah explained with فاتتني.
A closing تَقَبَّلَ اللهُ with its reply مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ, and جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا.
